# Errors

<!-- Generated by scripts/errdocs from internal/runner/errors.go; edit the
catalogue there and run task docs:errors. -->

Every error apic reports carries a stable code. A script or an agent can
branch on the code rather than on the wording of the message, which may
improve from release to release; a code never changes meaning, and new ones
are only added.

The first digit groups them: **E1xx** is the request as written, **E2xx**
the command and the project around it, **E3xx** the network. The exit
status follows from the code: 2 for E1xx and E2xx, 3 for E3xx (see
[exit codes](cli.md#exit-codes)). A failed assertion is not an error: it
exits 1 and is reported in the result.

## Where the code appears

On a terminal, under the message:

```text
error: auth.http:9: missing variable
  {{token}}: it is captured by request "login"; run `apic run login` first, or pass --var token=...
  E101 missing variable · see https://datagriff.github.io/api-caller/errors/#e101
```

With `--json`, as one object on **stderr** (stdout keeps only results, so a
pipe into `jq` is not disturbed):

```json
{"error":{"code":"E101","title":"missing variable","message":"auth.http:9: missing variable\n  {{token}}: it is captured by request …","hint":"Pass it with --var name=value, …","exit":2,"url":"https://datagriff.github.io/api-caller/errors/#e101"}}
```

Over [MCP](agents.md), a failed tool call carries the same object as its
structured content, and its text ends with the code, title and hint.

## E1xx: the request

<a id="e101"></a>

### E101 missing variable

Exit 2. A `{{placeholder}}` in the request has no value from any source: `--var`, the environment's entry in the env files, `.env`, the session, or a request earlier in the same run. The message names each missing variable and, when another request's `# @capture` provides it, that request. A `# @ref` to that request makes it run first by itself; `apic describe <request>` shows where every variable comes from.

**What to do:** Pass it with --var name=value, add it to an env file, or run the request that captures it first.

<a id="e102"></a>

### E102 request cannot be built

Exit 2. The request's text could not be turned into a request: a built-in with bad arguments (`{{$randomInt 5 1}}`), an unknown built-in, a URL that does not parse once its placeholders are filled in, or a GraphQL body whose variables are not a JSON object.

**What to do:** Check the placeholder, URL, header or body the message names.

<a id="e103"></a>

### E103 request file has errors

Exit 2. The `.http` file failed to parse where the request is: a malformed directive, a multipart body without a boundary, a GraphQL request without a query. apic refuses to send from a file with errors rather than guess; `apic validate` lists them all.

**What to do:** Run apic validate to see every problem with its line and column.

<a id="e104"></a>

### E104 bad directive value

Exit 2. A directive is well formed but its value cannot be used: `# @timeout soon`, `# @retry 0`, `# @sleep -1s`, an `# @assert` that does not parse, an HTTP version other than HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 on the request line, or `HTTP/2` over plain `http://`.

**What to do:** Fix the directive's value; docs/format.md lists what each takes.

<a id="e105"></a>

### E105 authentication failed

Exit 2. The request's auth could not be applied: an `# @auth` spec that does not parse, `# @auth exec` without `auth.allowExec`, an OAuth2 token endpoint that refused the grant, a browser sign-in with no terminal, or a JetBrains `Security.Auth` configuration that does not exist or cannot be used.

**What to do:** Check the # @auth spec (or auth.default), its credentials, and the token endpoint.

<a id="e106"></a>

### E106 body file problem

Exit 2. A file the request reads could not be used: a `< file` body, a multipart part's file, or a schema for `matchesSchema`. Paths are relative to the `.http` file and must resolve (symlinks included) inside the project root, so a request file cannot read something outside it.

**What to do:** Check that the file exists, relative to the .http file, and lies inside the project.

<a id="e107"></a>

### E107 @ref problem

Exit 2. A `# @ref` or `# @forceRef` names no request, several requests, or leads back to the request it started from. `apic validate` reports these as `bad-ref` and `ref-cycle` before anything runs.

**What to do:** Point # @ref at exactly one request, and break any cycle.

## E2xx: the command and project

<a id="e200"></a>

### E200 error

Exit 2. An error without a more specific code. It should be rare: if you meet one, the message is worth an issue so it can get a code of its own.

**What to do:** The message says what went wrong; if it is unclear, please open an issue.

<a id="e201"></a>

### E201 unknown request

Exit 2. The target names no request: no `# @name` of that name, no such `.http` file, or no request at that position in the file. The message suggests the closest names.

**What to do:** Run apic list to see the request ids, and use name, file.http, file.http#name or file.http#N.

<a id="e202"></a>

### E202 several requests match

Exit 2. The command works on one request (`describe`, `curl`, `snippet`) and the target names a whole file or a name used in several files.

**What to do:** Pick one with file.http#name, or give the command a single request.

<a id="e203"></a>

### E203 bad flag or argument

Exit 2. A flag has a value the command cannot use, two flags cannot be combined (`--output` with a flow or `--data`, `--use-session` with `--no-session`), an argument is missing or extra, or the command does not exist.

**What to do:** Check the command's flags with apic <command> --help.

<a id="e204"></a>

### E204 unknown environment

Exit 2. `--env` (or `env:` in `apic.yaml`) names an environment that neither env file declares, or there are no env files at all. `apic env` lists the environments found.

**What to do:** Use one of the environments the message lists, or add it to http-client.env.json.

<a id="e205"></a>

### E205 project configuration problem

Exit 2. The project could not be loaded: `apic.yaml` or an env file is not valid YAML/JSON, or a setting in it (a timeout, a retry policy) cannot be read.

**What to do:** Fix apic.yaml or the env file the message names; apic validate helps.

<a id="e206"></a>

### E206 TLS configuration problem

Exit 2. A TLS setting cannot be used: a CA file with no PEM certificates, a certificate or key that does not load, a key that is world-readable or needs a passphrase apic cannot supply, or a path outside the project.

**What to do:** Check the CA file, client certificate and key the message names.

<a id="e207"></a>

### E207 proxy configuration problem

Exit 2. `--proxy`, `proxy:` in `apic.yaml` or `HTTP(S)_PROXY` holds a URL apic cannot use. apic refuses the request rather than send it directly.

**What to do:** Give the proxy as an http, https, socks5 or socks5h URL.

<a id="e208"></a>

### E208 session or cookie store problem

Exit 2. `.apic/session.json` or the cookie jar could not be read or written, or a session command ran with `--no-session`.

**What to do:** Check .apic/ is writable, or run with --no-session.

<a id="e209"></a>

### E209 bad data file

Exit 2. The rows for `apic run --data` could not be read: an empty file, a header column without a name, a row with the wrong number of fields, or JSON that is not an array of objects.

**What to do:** Give --data a CSV file with a header row, or a JSON array of objects.

<a id="e210"></a>

### E210 cannot read or write a file

Exit 2. A file named on the command line (a report, a data file, a file to format, stdin) could not be read or written.

**What to do:** Check the path and its permissions.

<a id="e211"></a>

### E211 import failed

Exit 2. `apic import` could not read what it was given, or refused to overwrite files without `--force`.

**What to do:** Check the input is an OpenAPI 3 document, a Postman v2 collection or a curl command.

<a id="e212"></a>

### E212 feature file problem

Exit 2. `apic test` could not run the features: no `.feature` files, a feature that does not parse, an invalid tag expression, a step table or variable name it cannot use, or a step naming a target that is not a request.

**What to do:** Check the feature files, the step text and the tag expression.

<a id="e213"></a>

### E213 needs a terminal

Exit 2. `apic ui` is interactive: it refuses `--json` and a stdout that is not a terminal.

**What to do:** Run apic ui in a terminal; use apic run or apic list --json in scripts.

<a id="e214"></a>

### E214 server could not start

Exit 2. `apic mcp --http` or `apic demo` could not listen where it was asked to.

**What to do:** Check the address or port is free and allowed.

## E3xx: the network

<a id="e300"></a>

### E300 request failed

Exit 3. The request could not complete for a reason none of the E3xx codes below describes.

**What to do:** The message has the underlying error; check the URL and the network.

<a id="e301"></a>

### E301 could not connect

Exit 3. The host name did not resolve, the connection was refused or reset, or the network is unreachable. Nothing reached the server.

**What to do:** Check the host name, the port and that the server is running.

<a id="e302"></a>

### E302 timed out

Exit 3. The server did not answer within the timeout (30 seconds unless `--timeout`, `timeout:` in `apic.yaml` or `# @timeout` says otherwise).

**What to do:** Raise --timeout, # @timeout or timeout: in apic.yaml, or check the server.

<a id="e303"></a>

### E303 TLS handshake failed

Exit 3. The TLS handshake failed: the server's certificate is not trusted, has the wrong name or has expired, or the server refused the client certificate. `--insecure` skips verification for one command, as a last resort.

**What to do:** Trust the server's CA with --cacert or tls.caFile, or check the client certificate.

<a id="e304"></a>

### E304 protocol problem

Exit 3. The server's answer could not be used: it did not negotiate HTTP/2 for a request line that asks for it, the response was malformed, or the body was larger than apic reads.

**What to do:** Check the server speaks what the request asks for.

<a id="e305"></a>

### E305 cancelled

Exit 3. The run was interrupted (Ctrl-C, or `esc` in the UI) while a request, a `# @sleep` or a retry wait was in progress.

**What to do:** Run the command again.

## Validate diagnostics

`apic validate` reports problems in the files before anything runs, each
with a line, a column and one of these codes (the `code` key of
`validate --json`). They are a separate namespace from the E codes above:
a file with an error-severity diagnostic refuses to run with
[E103](#e103).

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ambiguous-step` | a `# @step` phrase that matches the same text as another step |
| `bad-assert` | `# @assert` that is not `selector op value` |
| `bad-auth` | an `# @auth` spec that does not parse |
| `bad-auth-config` | a JetBrains `Security.Auth` configuration in an env file that apic cannot use (not OAuth2, the Implicit grant, a missing Token URL or Client ID) |
| `bad-capture` | `# @capture` that is not `name = selector` |
| `bad-config-auth` | auth.default in apic.yaml does not parse |
| `bad-graphql` | a GraphQL request (GRAPHQL method or X-REQUEST-TYPE: GraphQL) without a query, or whose variables block is not a JSON object |
| `bad-header` | a line in the header section that is not `Name: value` |
| `bad-http-version` | a request line whose HTTP version is not HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 |
| `bad-multipart` | a multipart/form-data body without a boundary, or whose parts are not laid out between `--boundary` delimiters |
| `bad-name` | `# @name` without a value |
| `bad-ref` | a `# @ref` or `# @forceRef` whose target is not one request in the project |
| `bad-retry` | a `# @retry` (or retry in apic.yaml) that is not `<attempts> [interval]` |
| `bad-save-path` | a `>> file` after the body with no path, a path outside the project, or a second one on the same request |
| `bad-sleep` | a `# @sleep` whose value is not a duration such as 500ms or 2s |
| `bad-step` | a `# @step` phrase that does not parse |
| `duplicate-name` | a request name used more than once in the project |
| `editor-script` | an editor-only script or redirect block (skipped, not sent) |
| `exec-disabled` | `# @auth exec` without auth.allowExec in apic.yaml |
| `missing-body-file` | a `< file` body, or a `< file` part of a multipart body, whose file does not exist |
| `missing-schema-file` | a `# @assert … matchesSchema <file>` whose schema file does not exist or lies outside the project |
| `orphan-directives` | directives that are not followed by a request line |
| `ref-cycle` | a `# @ref` chain that leads back to the request it started from |
| `unknown-auth-key` | a field of a `Security.Auth` configuration that apic does not act on |
| `unknown-directive` | a `# @directive` apic does not know (ignored) |
| `unknown-selector` | a selector that is not status, statusText, duration, header.*, cookie.*, body or body.$*, or a body path apic cannot read |
